title: Flat ringed dg push-pull and its underlying-complex comparison
statement:
Let $X,Z$ be topological spaces with sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal O_X,\mathcal O_Z$. Let $f:X\to Z$ be continuous with a unital ring map $f^{-1}\mathcal O_Z\to\mathcal O_X$, and assume the module-sheaf pullback $f^*L=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Z}f^{-1}L$ is exact. Let $\mathcal C$ be a sheaf dg $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra and put $\mathcal B=f^*\mathcal C$, with multiplication induced by tensoring. Use left dg modules, signed shifts, cones and localization at underlying quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Assume the underlying complexes of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal B$ are K-flat over $\mathcal O_Z$ and $\mathcal O_X$, respectively [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Write $U_Z,U_X$ for their forgetful functors to the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Every sheaf dg $\mathcal B$-module has a quasi-isomorphism to a homotopically injective dg module $I$, meaning that the complex of global graded dg-linear maps from any acyclic dg module to $I$ is acyclic. Its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-complex is K-injective: the ordinary Hom complex from every acyclic $\mathcal O_X$-complex to $U_XI$ is acyclic. Degreewise $f_*I$, with its induced $\mathcal C$-action, computes an exact right derived functor $Rf_*^{\mathrm{dg}}$. There is an exact adjunction
$$f^*:D_Z(\mathcal C)\rightleftarrows D_X(\mathcal B):Rf_*^{\mathrm{dg}},$$
where dg pullback is the exact degreewise module-sheaf pullback. There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$U_X f^*\cong f^* U_Z,\qquad U_ZRf_*^{\mathrm{dg}}\cong Rf_*U_X.$$
Here $Rf_*$ is ordinary module-sheaf derived direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. Under these isomorphisms the dg adjunction unit and counit become the unit and counit of the ordinary exact-pullback/derived-pushforward adjunction. No boundedness of modules or cohomology is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0FT0 (theorem-qis-into-dg-injective), 0FRU (lemma-adjunction-push-pull-dg), and 0FTR (lemma-derived-adjoint-push-pull). The K-flat forgetful comparison and compatibility with the ordinary adjunction are the stated agent refinement.

proof.text: Apply the Grothendieck-category and acyclic-test lemmas to $\mathcal B$. Fix the resulting set $a_r:E_r\hookrightarrow F_r$ of acyclic dg modules. For a dg module $M$, let $T(M)$ be the pushout of $\bigoplus_{(r,u)}E_r\to\bigoplus_{(r,u)}F_r$ along the evaluation map to $M$, where $u$ ranges over dg maps $E_r\to M$. These are set-indexed coproducts. The induced map $j_M:M\hookrightarrow T(M)$ is monic and has cokernel $\bigoplus_{(r,u)}\operatorname{coker}(a_r)$: this follows by computing the pushout as the quotient of $M\oplus\bigoplus F_r$ by $(u(e),-a_r(e))$. Each $\operatorname{coker}(a_r)$ is acyclic by the long exact cohomology sequence, and their coproduct is acyclic since it is the filtered colimit of finite sums and cohomology commutes with filtered colimits. Another long exact sequence gives that $j_M$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Every $u:E_r\to M$ extends across $F_r$ into $T(M)$ by its coproduct summand. Postcomposition of $u$ defines the summand maps for $T(M)\to T(M')$, so $T$ and $j$ are functorial.

Choose a limit ordinal $\alpha$ of cofinality larger than the cardinality of the subobject set of each $E_r$, possible because $R$ is a set. Set $M_0=M$, $M_{\beta+1}=T(M_\beta)$, and $M_\lambda=\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\lambda}M_\beta$ at limits. The transition maps are monic quasi-isomorphisms: successor maps were checked above; at limits, exact filtered colimits and their cohomology compatibility give the same assertion. In particular $M\to I=M_\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Smallness of each $E_r$ in this Grothendieck category says that every $u:E_r\to I$ factors through some $M_\beta$, $\beta<\alpha$. Its map into $M_{\beta+1}$ extends to $F_r$ by the preceding construction, and $\beta+1<\alpha$. Hence $u$ extends to $F_r\to I$, and the test lemma makes $I$ graded injective and homotopically injective. Recursion on the functor $T$ makes $M\to I$ functorial. The construction applies equally to $\mathcal C$ and involves no degree bound.

source.place: Tag 0FT0, theorem-qis-into-dg-injective, successor and limit stages; Injectives Tag 079F.

proof.text: For an acyclic $\mathcal O_X$-complex $L$, the free/forgetful specialization of the Hom-complex adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal O_X}(L,U_XI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L,I)$. The underlying free-module complex is acyclic by K-flatness of $\mathcal B$: the tensor symmetry $b\otimes l\mapsto(-1)^{|b||l|}l\otimes b$ identifies it with the tensor in the definition of K-flatness. The right Hom complex is acyclic by homotopical injectivity of $I$. Thus $U_XI$ is K-injective. This applies to every homotopically injective $I$, and the identical argument with $\mathcal C$ gives the corresponding assertion on $Z$.

source.place: Agent refinement of 0FT0: free/forgetful adjunction and K-flatness of the algebra.

proof.text: Use the sheaf dg homotopy-system theorem and triangulated localization for $K_X(\mathcal B)$ and $D_X(\mathcal B)$. The right-module version applies to left modules by $m\cdot a=(-1)^{|a||m|}am$ over the graded opposite algebra; this changes right shifts to the stated signed left shifts. Acyclic dg modules form a full triangulated subcategory since their underlying cones and shifts are acyclic. A homotopically injective $I$ is right orthogonal to that subcategory, since $H^0\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(E,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K_X(\mathcal B)}(E,I)=0$. The orthogonal-localization lemma gives natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{K_X(\mathcal B)}(N,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D_X(\mathcal B)}(QN,QI)$. Thus localization is fully faithful on homotopically injectives and essentially surjective by step 2. Those objects are closed under shifts and cones: Hom into a shifted object is the shifted Hom complex, and Hom into a cone is the cone of the Hom map, hence acyclic for acyclic input. Their full subcategory therefore maps by an exact equivalence to $D_X(\mathcal B)$. The same statements hold on $Z$.

The underived adjunction identifies dg pullback with exact degreewise ordinary pullback because $\mathcal B=f^*\mathcal C$. Exactness implies that this functor preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms; hence it descends to $f^*$ on derived categories. The Hom-complex adjunction shows that $f_*I$ is homotopically injective over $\mathcal C$: for acyclic $N$, its Hom complex into $f_*I$ equals that from the acyclic $f^*N$ into $I$. Define $Rf_*^{\mathrm{dg}}$ by the inverse of the equivalence in step 4, followed by $f_*$ and localization. It is represented by $f_*I$ for every resolution in step 2. Shifts and cones are preserved by $f_*$ on the homotopy category, and the equivalence and localization are exact; therefore $Rf_*^{\mathrm{dg}}$ is exact. The same cone calculation makes the descended $f^*$ exact.

source.place: Tags 0FRU, 0FT5; section-derived-pushforward, computation on injective representatives.

proof.text: For completeness the construction is a total right derived functor, with its usual comparison: the inclusion of the homotopically injective subcategory followed by the inverse equivalence defines $r:D_X(\mathcal B)\to K_X(\mathcal B)$. Step 4 gives $Q\dashv r$, with unit represented by $M\to I$ and invertible counit $Qr\cong\mathrm{id}$. Put $H=Q_{\mathcal C}f_*$. Then $Hr=Rf_*^{\mathrm{dg}}$, and $H\to HrQ$ is $H$ applied to this unit. For any functor $V$ on $D_X(\mathcal B)$, a transformation $a:H\to VQ$ determines $Hr\xrightarrow{ar}VQr\to V$ using the counit, and a transformation $b:Hr\to V$ gives $H\to HrQ\xrightarrow{bQ}VQ$. The two composites are identities by the adjunction triangle identities. The argument works after arbitrary postcomposition, so the derived functor is absolute. Its comparison on a homotopically injective object is invertible.

source.place: Section-derived-pushforward, lemma-right-derived; explicit Kan universal property from the equivalence in step 4.

proof.text:
For $N$ on $Z$ and a resolution $M\to I$ on $X$, use step 4, the underived Hom adjunction, and the homotopical injectivity of $f_*I$ to obtain natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D_X(\mathcal B)}(f^*N,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K_X(\mathcal B)}(f^*N,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K_Z(\mathcal C)}(N,f_*I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D_Z(\mathcal C)}(N,Rf_*^{\mathrm{dg}}M).$$
They define the required adjunction. Each bijection commutes with the signed shifts (it is induced by the Hom-complex isomorphism and localization), so this is an exact adjunction with the exact functors of step 5. Its maps are the derived unit and counit of the underived adjunction, since the middle bijection is precisely that adjunction, with its specified evaluation formulas.

source.place: Tag 0FTR, lemma-derived-adjoint-push-pull, specialized to exact pullback.

proof.text: The underived pullback tensor identification is literally the same underlying ordinary pullback complex, natural in chain maps and homotopies; it inverts the same quasi-isomorphisms. It therefore gives $U_Xf^*\cong f^*U_Z$. By step 3, $U_XM\to U_XI$ is an ordinary K-injective resolution. The ordinary derived-direct-image definition computes $Rf_*U_XM$ as $f_*U_XI$, while the other composite is $U_Z(f_*I)$, the same complex with the same differential. The canonical comparison between these representatives is the identity. For maps, step 4 represents derived arrows into a resolution by dg homotopy classes; forgetting gives the ordinary homotopy classes representing the same derived arrows by the ordinary K-injective Hom theorem. Thus the identity comparisons commute with all derived maps and with replacement of $I$, giving the canonical natural isomorphism $U_ZRf_*^{\mathrm{dg}}\cong Rf_*U_X$.

source.place: Tag 0FTW, lemma-pushforward-agrees, using the stronger K-flat representative comparison.

proof.text: Check the adjunction maps under these comparisons, rather than only identifying the functors. Take $M\to I$ as above. After forgetting actions, $f_*U_XI$ is an ordinary K-injective complex: apply the Hom adjunction of the underived lemma with dg algebras $\mathcal O_Z,\mathcal O_X$ concentrated in degree zero, and use exactness of ordinary $f^*$ and K-injectivity of $U_XI$. Consequently the ordinary adjunction is computed by the same three Hom bijections as step 7 after forgetting the actions, using ordinary K-injective localization on both sides. This square of Hom correspondences commutes, because the underived lemma's tensor identification sends the dg unit $n\mapsto1\otimes n$ and evaluation counit to the ordinary ones. Applying the square to the identity of $f^*N$ gives equality of the two units, and applying it to the identity of $Rf_*^{\mathrm{dg}}M$ gives equality of the two counits. All constructions use arbitrary integer complexes; no truncation or boundedness assumption occurred.
